rules.//: Default deny. Every path below is opened deliberately; anything not listed stays unreadable and unwritable, including the root itself.

chats.//: No listing of /chats. A chat is reachable only by its own id, and only by the people named in it.

$chatId..read: auth != null && (root.child('chats/' + $chatId + '/participants/customer').val() === auth.uid || root.child('chats/' + $chatId + '/participants/technician').val() === auth.uid || root.child('chats/' + $chatId + '/participants/admin').val() === auth.uid || root.child('chats/' + $chatId + '/participants/' + auth.uid).exists())
$chatId.//write: An existing chat is writable by its participants. A new one is writable only by someone who names themselves in it, so no one can create a chat on behalf of another person. The trailing clause of each branch accepts the legacy uid -> role maps that predate role-keyed participants.
$chatId..write: auth != null && ((data.exists() && (data.child('participants/customer').val() === auth.uid || data.child('participants/technician').val() === auth.uid || data.child('participants/admin').val() === auth.uid || data.child('participants/' + auth.uid).exists())) || (!data.exists() && (newData.child('participants/customer').val() === auth.uid || newData.child('participants/technician').val() === auth.uid || newData.child('participants/admin').val() === auth.uid || newData.child('participants/' + auth.uid).exists())))
$chatId.//validate: Every chat must name its participants and its booking. This is what stops markAsRead conjuring a counter-only stub: a write to chats/<id>/customerUnreadCount on a missing chat now fails instead of creating a chat that names nobody.

$messageId.//write: Participants may append a message, delete one they sent, or edit an existing one - and the per-field rules below narrow editing down to the status field alone, because every other field is frozen once written.
$messageId..write: auth != null && (root.child('chats/' + $chatId + '/participants/customer').val() === auth.uid || root.child('chats/' + $chatId + '/participants/technician').val() === auth.uid || root.child('chats/' + $chatId + '/participants/admin').val() === auth.uid || root.child('chats/' + $chatId + '/participants/' + auth.uid).exists()) && ((!data.exists() && newData.child('senderId').val() === auth.uid) || (!newData.exists() && data.child('senderId').val() === auth.uid) || (data.exists() && newData.exists()))
$messageId.//senderId: You may only write your own uid as the sender, and it can never change afterwards - so a message cannot be forged under another name, nor reattributed later.

userChats.//: A chat list is private to its owner, but either participant may write into the entry belonging to the other - that is how a sender bumps the recipient unread count and message preview. Both sides must be participants of that chat, so nobody can plant entries in the list of a stranger.
